text:
Dina: Quick share — ran a SmoothQuant vs AWQ/GPTQ sweep on 7B/13B with 32k context this morning. TL;DR: SmoothQuant + AWQ act-aware looks like the best quality/cost tradeoff so far, FP8 matches baseline but is "noisy on edge cases".

Sam: Nice. what metrics did you track?

Dina: PPL, MRR@5 on conveval dev set, token-level exact-match for code snippets, and a small human pass on 200 prompts. Also tracked tokens/sec and GPU mem.

Sam: numbers?

Dina: Short table in text form:
- 7B FP16 baseline: PPL 12.1, MRR@5 0.72,  tokens/sec 210, GPU 12.6GB
- 7B GPTQ-INT8: PPL 13.4 (+10.7%), MRR 0.69, tokens/sec 320, GPU 7.2GB
- 7B AWQ-actaware-INT8: PPL 12.5 (+3.3%), MRR 0.71, tokens/sec 310, GPU 7.4GB
- 7B SmoothQuant+AWQ-INT8: PPL 12.3 (+1.6%), MRR 0.715, tokens/sec 300, GPU 7.6GB
- 7B FP8 (mixed e4m3): PPL 12.2 (+0.8%), MRR 0.719, tokens/sec 360, GPU 6.9GB

For 13B similar pattern but deltas larger: GPTQ had ~15% PPL increase at 32k, AWQ-actaware ~5-7%, SmoothQuant+AWQ ~2.5%, FP8 ~1.2%.

Kyle: Interesting that FP8 is close but "noisy on edge cases" — what do you mean?

Dina: Some long-code generation prompts (very long prefix with syntactic nesting) produced token-level hallucinations: incorrect indent/closing braces that human eval flagged. Those were concentrated in cases where activation distributions spiked (checked layer 18/20 on 13B).

Anika: Did you try activation clipping or per-channel scaling?

Dina: Yes. Two quick experiments: 1) per-channel quantization (GPTQ style) reduced some hallucinations but regressed average PPL due to quantization noise on small-weight matrices. 2) activation clipping (99.9 percentile) helped AWQ but made FP8 unstable in ~2% of samples.

Matt: Can you paste the commands/configs you used?

Dina: Sure — main quant flow we ran:
```
python quantize.py --model rwi-13b --method smoothquant --act-aware --bits 8 --context 32768 --kv-warmup 512 --block-size 1024 --batch 1
python eval.py --dataset conveval --metrics ppl,mrr,exact --max-toks 32768
```
Also ran FP8 with the runtime patch: set ENV FP8_HW=1 and quantizer bits e4m3.

Sam: How were you loading KV cache for long context? cold start or streaming?

Dina: Cold start in these runs. Noted that when we pre-warm KV cache with a 2k token primer the GPTQ errors reduced slightly but AWQ/ SmoothQuant stayed stable — suggests GPTQ sensitivity to prefix scaling.

Kyle: Any latency/regression surprises?

Dina: Throughput improved as expected on INT8/FP8 but tail latency occasionally jumps when attention patterns cause large activation peaks (layer 18). Saw a 30–80ms spike at ~95th percentile on some samples.

Anika: Did you inspect quantization scales during those spikes?

Dina: Yes. Dumped layer scales for a failing prompt — found one head with activation scale 3x larger than baseline causing quantizer saturation. SmoothQuant's activation scaling reduced that head's effective scale and avoided saturation.

ci-bot: CI: longctx-regression-test (rwi-13b) started by Dina at 1769457001

Dina: A couple of low-level observations:
- SmoothQuant helps when activation and weight outliers are correlated — it rescales activations to be quant-friendly.
- AWQ's act-aware rounding improves per-token fidelity vs straight GPTQ in long prefixes.
- FP8 gives best memory and throughput but requires per-workload clipping heuristics to avoid the edge-case hallucinations.

Sam: For production canaries, what do you recommend?

Dina: Plan: canary SmoothQuant+AWQ-int8 on a small dedicated pool with these safety nets:
- rate-limit to 5 TPS initially
- shadow baseline FP16 for randomized 1% of requests and automatic rollback on PPL delta > 3% or human complaint rate > 0.5/1000
- warm KV cache for first 2 tokens by sending primer context for known high-length routes

Kyle: Good. Also add auto-fallback to FP16 on observed scale spikes > 2.5x on any internal layer. We can implement that in runtime router.

Anika: For the next sweep I suggest:
- try per-channel vs per-tensor AWQ mixing (hybrid)
- run with cold, warmed (2k primer), and fully streamed contexts
- increase block-size to 2048 to see batching tradeoff

Dina: Agreed. I'll schedule runs overnight and push a summary tomorrow. Will also dump per-layer scale logs and attach a small analysis notebook.

Matt: Awesome. If the canary looks stable we can add a beta flag in Redwood Console for teams to opt into reduced-cost INT8 routes.

Sam: Thanks Dina. ping us when the overnight sweep finishes. :thumbsup:

Dina: Will do. Thanks all.
